p01222.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 3
p01222.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. III, sig. 113a–114a
p01222.modern: This partition and portion of Japheth, with the part which he held in Asia, and the North, which was also very great, answers to that blessing of God by Noah. Dilatet Deus ("Noah. May God enlarge.") JAPHETH; Let God spread abroad( or increase the posterity of) Japheth, and let him dwell in the Tents of SHEM. For though Junius Iunius here uses the word( 〈◊ 〉) and not dilatet: and the Genevapersuadeat Geneuapersuadeat; yet the Septuagint have dilatet or amplificet; and such was the blessing given to our Fathers, which God promised to Abraham and his seed for ever. And the dwelling in the Tents or Tabernacles of Shem was a blessing by God to the posterity of Japheth: noting not only an enlargement of Territories; but that thereby they should be made participant of Gods Church. But to come to Japhets sons, of whom Gomer is the eldest. This Gomer( if we may believe Berosus and Annius, whose authority the greatest number of all our late Writers have followed) did in the tenth year of Nimrods reign depart from Babylonia, and planted Italy: which also Funck Functius confirms in these words: Anno decimo NIMRODI, &c. In the tenth year of Nimrods reign, GOMER GOMERVS GALLUS planted a Colony in that land afterward called Italy: and in the twelfth year of the same Nimrods reign TUBAL seated himself in Asturia in Spain( now called Biscay) which was in the 140. and in the 142. years after the Flood, according to BEROSUS. But this opinion is very ridiculous. For before the confusion of tongues the children of Noah did not separate themselves, at least So many of them as came with Nimrod into Shinar. Let us therefore consider with reason, what time the building such a City and Tower required, where there was no prepared matter, nor any ready means to perform such a work as Nimrod had erected( and as Funck himself out of his Author Berosus witnesses) ad altitudinem & magnitudinem montium; To the height and magnitude of the Mountains Mountaines. Sure that both this City and Tower were almost built the Scriptures witness: But the Lord came down to see the City and Tower, which the Sons of men built. Let us then but allot a time sufficient for the making of Brick to such a Work, of the greatest height( and therefore of circuit and foundation answerable) that ever was. For where the universal Flood covered the highest Mountains fifteen Cubits; Let us build us a City and a Tower( says Nimrod) whose top may reach unto the Heaven: meaning, that they would rays their Work above fifteen Cubits higher then the highest Mountain, otherwise they could not assure themselves from the fear of a second inundation: a great part whereof was finished before it fell, and before they left the Work. They also began this building upon a ground, the most oppressed with waters of all the World: as by the great ruin which these waters forcibly over-bearing and over-flowing, made in the time of the succeeding Emperors Emperours, is made manifest, approved also by the Prophet Jeremiah Hieremie, speaking of Babylon in these words: Thou that dwellest upon many waters. It cannot be doubted but that there needed a substantial foundation, for So high a raised building on a marsh ground: and to which, Glycas upon Genesis gives forty years. For it seems, that the Tower was near finished when God overthrew it: it being afterward written, So the Lord scattered them from thence upon all the earth, and they left to build the City. Out of which place it may be gathered( because the Tower is not then named) that they very near had performed the Work of their supposed defence, which was the Tower: and that afterward they went on with the City adjoining, wherein they inhabited. It is also to be noted, that till such time as this confusion seized them( whereupon the Tower was thrown down) these Nations did not disperse themselves: for from thence the Lord scattered them upon all the Earth, ( that was) when they perceived not one another's speech. Now to think that this Work in the newness of the World( wanting all instruments and materials) could be performed in ten years; and that Tubal and Gomer in the same year could creep through 3000. miles of Desert, with Women, Children, and Cattle: let those light Believers Beleeuers, that neither tie themselves to the Scripture, nor to reason, approve it, for I do not. And if the Ark of Noah was 100. years in building, or but near such a time, ( and then) when the World had stood 1556. years, it were more than foolishness and madness it self, to think that such a Work as this could be performed in ten; when the World( from the Flood to the arrival at Babel, and beginning of this building there) had but 131. years, and whereof they had spent some part in travailing from the East. Again, if all Asia set to their helping hands in the building of the Temple of Diana, and yet they consumed in that Work 400. years( or be it but half that time) and in such an Age as when the World flourished in all sorts of Artificers, and with abundant plenty of materials and carriages: This Work of the Tower of Babel could hardly( with all the former wants supposed) be erected in those few years remembered. And for conclusion, let all men of judgement weigh with themselves how impossible it was for a Nation or Family of men, with their Wives Wiues and Children, and Cattle, to travail 3000. miles through Woods, Bogs, and Deserts Desarts, without any Guide or Conductor; and we shall find it rather a Work of 100. years then of 100. days. For in the West Indies of which the Spaniards have the experience, in those places where they found neither path nor Guide, they have not entered the Country ten miles in ten years. And if Nimrods people spent many years by the account before remembered in passing from the East-India or the higher part thereof, which stands in 115. Degrees of Longitude, until they came into Shinar which lies in 79. Degrees( the distance between those places containing 36. Degrees, which make 720. Leagues, which is 2160. miles) and did all the way keep the Mountains and hard ground; then the difference between Babylon and Biscay is much more: for the body of Biscay lies in ten Degrees, and Babylon or Shinar, ( as aforesaid) in 79. So the length of way from Shinar to Asturia or Biscay is 69. Degrees, which make 1380. Leagues, or of miles 4140. And therefore if Nimrod took divers years to find Shinar, which was but 2160. miles: or( supposing that the Ark rested in Armenia) little above 400. miles: there is no cause to the contrary, but to allow as many years to Gomer and Tubal to travail 3000. miles to Countries less known unto them by far; then the Land of Shinar was to Nimrod. For Paradise was known to Noah before the Flood: and So was the Region of Eden by Moses afterward remembered; but what he understood of most part of the World else it is unknown. And therefore did Annius ill advise himself to plant Gomer in Italy, and Tubal in Spain, in the tenth and twelfth of Nimrods Reign: Shall the earth be brought forth in one day, or shall a Nation be borne at one? But it may be objected, That the Sons of Japheth might come by Sea, and So save this great travail through Deserts by Land. But we never read of any Navigation in those days, nor long after. Surely he that knows what it is to embark So great a people as we may justly suppose those Conductors Conducters carried with them, will not easily believe, that there were any Vessels in those days to transport Armies, and( withal) their Cattle, by whose Milk they lived and fed their Children: for Milk and Fruit were the banqueting dishes of our Forefathers. And in the eldest times, even the Kings and Fathers of Nations valued themselves by the Herds Heards and numbers of their Cattel: who had flocks of Sheep, and great Droves Droues and Herds of their own, and their own Sheep-herds Sheep-heards and Heardsmen. Now if Tubal had past by Sea from any part of Palestine Palaestina, Syria, or Cilicia, he might have made good choice within the Straits Streights, and not have gone beyond Granado, Valentia, and other Provinces Prouinces in that Tract: past the Straits of Gibralter, disdained all Andalusia and Portugal, with all those goodly Ports and Countries; and have sought out the iron, woody, and barren Country of the World( called Biscay) by a long and dangerous Navigation. But before the journey of the Argonauts Argonautae there were scarce any Vessels that durst cross the Seas in that part of the World: and yet that which Jason had( if the Tale be true) was but a Galley, and a poor one( God knows) and perchance such as they use this day in Ireland: which although it carried but four and fifty Passengers, yet was it far greater than any of the former times: Erat enim antea paruarum ("For before [it was] of small [cities];") navicularum usus: For in former times they used very small Vessels. I deny not but that the Tyrians gave themselves of old to far-off Navigations Nauigations, whence Tibullus ascribed the invention of Ships unto them:

Let us then but allot a time sufficient for the making of Brick to such a Work, of the greatest height( and therefore of circuit and foundation answerable) that ever was. For where the universal Flood covered the highest Mountains fifteen Cubits; Let us build us a City and a Tower( says Nimrod) whose top may reach unto the Heaven: meaning, that they would rays their Work above fifteen Cubits higher then the highest Mountain, otherwise they could not assure themselves from the fear of a second inundation: a great part whereof was finished before it fell, and before they left the Work. They also began this building upon a ground, the most oppressed with waters of all the World: as by the great ruin which these waters forcibly over-bearing and over-flowing, made in the time of the succeeding Emperors, is made manifest, approved also by the Prophet Jeremiah, speaking of Babylon in these words: Thou that dwellest upon many waters. It cannot be doubted but that there needed a substantial foundation, for So high a raised building on a marsh ground: and to which, Glycas upon Genesis gives forty years. For it seems, that the Tower was near finished when God overthrew it: it being afterward written, So the Lord scattered them from thence upon all the earth, and they left to build the City. Out of which place it may be gathered( because the Tower is not then named) that they very near had performed the Work of their supposed defence, which was the Tower: and that afterward they went on with the City adjoining, wherein they inhabited. It is also to be noted, that till such time as this confusion seized them( whereupon the Tower was thrown down) these Nations did not disperse themselves: for from thence the Lord scattered them upon all the Earth, ( that was) when they perceived not one another's speech. Now to think that this Work in the newness of the World( wanting all instruments and materials) could be performed in ten years; and that Tubal and Gomer in the same year could creep through 3000. miles of Desert, with Women, Children, and Cattle: let those light Believers, that neither tie themselves to the Scripture, nor to reason, approve it, for I do not. And if the Ark of Noah was 100. years in building, or but near such a time, ( and then) when the World had stood 1556. years, it were more than foolishness and madness it self, to think that such a Work as this could be performed in ten; when the World( from the Flood to the arrival at Babel, and beginning of this building there) had but 131. years, and whereof they had spent some part in travailing from the East. Again, if all Asia set to their helping hands in the building of the Temple of Diana, and yet they consumed in that Work 400. years( or be it but half that time) and in such an Age as when the World flourished in all sorts of Artificers, and with abundant plenty of materials and carriages: This Work of the Tower of Babel could hardly( with all the former wants supposed) be erected in those few years remembered. And for conclusion, let all men of judgement weigh with themselves how impossible it was for a Nation or Family of men, with their Wives and Children, and Cattle, to travail 3000. miles through Woods, Bogs, and Deserts, without any Guide or Conductor; and we shall find it rather a Work of 100. years then of 100. days. For in the West Indies of which the Spaniards have the experience, in those places where they found neither path nor Guide, they have not entered the Country ten miles in ten years. And if Nimrods people spent many years by the account before remembered in passing from the East-India or the higher part thereof, which stands in 115. Degrees of Longitude, until they came into Shinar which lies in 79. Degrees( the distance between those places containing 36. Degrees, which make 720. Leagues, which is 2160. miles) and did all the way keep the Mountains and hard ground; then the difference between Babylon and Biscay is much more: for the body of Biscay lies in ten Degrees, and Babylon or Shinar, ( as aforesaid) in 79. So the length of way from Shinar to Asturia or Biscay is 69. Degrees, which make 1380. Leagues, or of miles 4140. And therefore if Nimrod took divers years to find Shinar, which was but 2160. miles: or( supposing that the Ark rested in Armenia) little above 400. miles: there is no cause to the contrary, but to allow as many years to Gomer and Tubal to travail 3000. miles to Countries less known unto them by far; then the Land of Shinar was to Nimrod. For Paradise was known to Noah before the Flood: and So was the Region of Eden by Moses afterward remembered; but what he understood of most part of the World else it is unknown. And therefore did Annius ill advise himself to plant Gomer in Italy, and Tubal in Spain, in the tenth and twelfth of Nimrods Reign: Shall the earth be brought forth in one day, or shall a Nation be borne at one? But it may be objected, That the Sons of Japheth might come by Sea, and So save this great travail through Deserts by Land. But we never read of any Navigation in those days, nor long after. Surely he that knows what it is to embark So great a people as we may justly suppose those Conductors carried with them, will not easily believe, that there were any Vessels in those days to transport Armies, and( withal) their Cattle, by whose Milk they lived and fed their Children: for Milk and Fruit were the banqueting dishes of our Forefathers. And in the eldest times, even the Kings and Fathers of Nations valued themselves by the Herds and numbers of their Cattel: who had flocks of Sheep, and great Droves and Herds of their own, and their own Sheep-herds and Heardsmen. Now if Tubal had past by Sea from any part of Palestine, Syria, or Cilicia, he might have made good choice within the Straits, and not have gone beyond Granado, Valentia, and other Provinces in that Tract: past the Straits of Gibralter, disdained all Andalusia and Portugal, with all those goodly Ports and Countries; and have sought out the iron, woody, and barren Country of the World( called Biscay) by a long and dangerous Navigation. But before the journey of the Argonauts there were scarce any Vessels that durst cross the Seas in that part of the World: and yet that which Jason had( if the Tale be true) was but a Galley, and a poor one( God knows) and perchance such as they use this day in Ireland: which although it carried but four and fifty Passengers, yet was it far greater than any of the former times: Erat enim antea paruarum navicularum usus: For in former times they used very small Vessels. I deny not but that the Tyrians gave themselves of old to far-off Navigations, whence Tibullus ascribed the invention of Ships unto them:

p01224.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 3
p01224.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. III, sig. 114b
p01224.modern: And although it cannot be denied, when Noah by Gods inspiration was instructed in So many particulars concerning the Ark, that then many things concerning Navigation were first revealed; yet it appears that there was much difference between the Ark of Noah, and such Ships as were for any long Navigation. Yea ancient Stories show, that it was long after these times, ere any durst presume upon any long Voyages to Sea: at least with multitudes of Women, and Children, and Cattle: as also common reason can tell us, that even now when this Art is come to her perfection, such Voyages Voiages are very troublesome and dangerous. So as it does appear, that there was not in that Age of Nimrod any Ship, or use of Ships fit for any long Navigation. For if Gomer and Tubal had passed themselves and their people by Sea; the exercise of Navigation would not have been dead for So many hundred years after. Leaving therefore the fabulous to their Fables, and all men else to their fancies, who have cast Nations into Countries far off, I know not how, I will follow herein the Relation of Moses and the Prophets: to which Truth there is joined both Nature, Reason, Policy, and necessity: and to the rest, neither probability, nor possibility.

p01226.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. IV, sig. 114b–115a
p01226.modern: Now although many learned and reverend men have formed( I know not whereby led) a Plantation of the World, which also has been and is received: yet I hope I may be excused, if I differ altogether from them in many particulars. Certainly, that great learned man of this latter Age, Arias Montanus was also in some things much mistaken: and for Josephus Iosephus, as he has many good things, and is a Guide to many errors withal, So was he in this Plantation of the World very gross and fabulous, whereby both Eusebius, Hierosolymitanus, Epiphanius, and others, that have taken his testimonies for currant, have been by him far misted. But the better to conceive what Regions of the World Gomer the first son of Japheth Iaphet possessed, as also Tubal, it is needful to begin with Magog: because the Scriptures take most knowledge of Gog and Magog, which two names have troubled many Commentators, says Matth. Beroaldo Beroaldus, who has laboured herein with great diligence, and whom( of all that ever I read) I find most judicious in the examination of this plantation. He takes authority from the Prophet Ezekiel chiefly, who in the 38: and 39: Chapter directs us, what Nations the Gomerians, Tubalines, and Togormians were, together with the Magogians: of which Gog was Prince or chief Conductor in their attempts against Israel. For besides the portions of Europe, and the North-east parts of the greater Asia, which Japheths Iapheths issues possessed, all Asia the less was peopled by them. And that those of the issue of Japheth( whom Ezekiel speaks of) were seated hereabout, it may best appear, if we consider the circumstances of the place, and the dependency upon the former prophecy in the 37. Chapter. For in that 37. Chapter, Ezekiel prophesies of the uniting of the two Kingdoms Kingdomes of Israel and Judah Iuda, after their delivery from Captivity captiuitie.

p01227.modern: By which prophecy of Ezekiel, it appears, that God purposed to gather together his people, to give life to dead bones, and to rule them by one Prince. For to that purpose it is written; And DAVID my servant shall be King over them, and they shall have one sheep-heard, ( that is) they shall be united as they were in Davids Dauids time. Hereupon in the 38. Chapter Ezekiel prophesies against those Nations, which should seek to impeach this Union, and disturb the people of Israel, whom God purposed to receive to grace, and promised to restore. And So in the same Chapter are those Nations coupled together, which infested the Israelites after their return, and sought to subject them: all which were the subjects or Allies of Gog, Prince of the Magogians, or Coelesyrians, next bordering Palestine Palaestina, or the holy Land, followed also by the rest of the Nations of Asia the less, which lay North from Judea Iudaea. The words of Ezekiel are these: Son of man, set thy face against GOG, and against the land of MAGOG, the chief Princes of Meshech( or MOSOCH and TUBAL: and afterward; Behold, I come against the chief Prince of MESHECH and TUBAL: and in the sixth Verse; GOMER and all his bands, and the house of Togarmah TOGORMA of the North quarters. Herein Ezekiel having first delivered the purpose of his Prophecy, teaches what Nations they were, that should in vain assail Israel. he joins Heioyneth them together under their Prince Gog, and shows that their habitations were on the North quarters of Judah, and how seated and joined together. Gog signifies in the Hebrew( says Saint Jerome Hierome) tectum or covering of a house: and Pintus upon Ezekiel affirms, that by Gog is meant Antichrist: for( says he) Antichrist us erit Diabolitegumentum sub specie humana: That Antichrist shall be the covering of the Devil under humane form. He adds that Magog is as much to say as Gog: the letter ( M) being an Hebrew Preposition, and imports as much as of or from: So he takes Magog for those people which follow Antichrist. So far Pintus; at least in this not amiss, that he expounds Magog not for any one person, but for a Nation, with which agrees this observation of Beroaldo. Magog( says he) in Hebrew is written Ham-Magog, which shows Magog to be a Region or Nation: for the letter( He) which is used but for an Emphasis( which the Hebrews Hebrewes call Heliaiedia) is never added to proper names of men, but often to place. So as Gog was Prince of that Nation( called either Magog, or according to others, the people of Gog) also Prince of Meshech, ( or Mosoch) and of Tubal: as by the first Verse of the 39. Chapter is made manifest: Behold, I come against thee GOG the chief Prince of MESHECH and TUBAL. This must needs be meant by the Successors Successours of Seleucus 〈◊ 〉, who did not( as other conquering Nations) seek to make the Jews Iewes their 〈◊ 〉 only, but endeavoured by all means, and by all kind of violence to extinguish the Religion it self( which the Hebrews professed) and the acknowledging of one true God: and to force them to worship and serve the mortal and rotten gods of the Heathen; of which nothing remained but the very name, and dead Images. S. 〈◊ 〉 and Isidore take Gog for the Nation of the Goths: probably because they invaded Europe, and sacked Rome, and many other places and Cities thereabout. 〈◊ 〉 〈◊ 〉 out of Pomp. Mela derives the Turks Turkes from the Scythians, esteemed Magoqueians of Gog Many take Gog for the proper name of a Man: other of a Region: others for a Nation inhabiting a Region, as Junius Iunius, who says that Gog is the name of a Nation, denominated from him whom the Greek Greeke Stories call Gyges: who in former time having slain Candaules the Lydian, gave his own name to that Nation, thence after called Gygades: and thereof also the Gygean Lake; which Lake Strabo also finds in Lydia, ( of which Gyges was King) forty Furlongs from Sardis. Pliny Plinie calls it Gygeum stagnum. Herodotus and Nicander set it about the Rivers Riuers of 〈◊ 〉, and Moeander; but the difference is not great. Marius Niger makes mention of this Gyges King of Lydia: who after he had subdued the Country about the River Rhodius which runs into the Hellespont, called the Promontory Trapes after his own name Gyges. These opinions do also seem to strengthen that of Junius. For Magog, says he, is that part of Asia the less, which Alyattes Halyattes obtained, and after him his son Croesus; who( as Junius further notes) having mastered all those Regions as far South as Lebanon Libanus in that border built the City Gigarta or Gogkarta( which in the Syrian signifies the City of Gog) seated in 〈◊ 〉, whose people were the ancient Enemies of the Jews.

p01228.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 4
p01228.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. IV, sig. 115b
p01228.modern: Now that Magog is found in Coelesyria, Pliny affirms, saying; 〈◊ 〉 habet Bambycen, quaealio nomine Hierapo ' is vocatur, 〈◊ 〉 vero Magog. Coelesyria has in it Bambyce, which by another name is called Hierapolis, but of the Syrians Magog. He further tells us that the monstrous Idol 〈◊ 〉, called by the Greeks Greekes Derceto, was here worshipped, Lucian makes mention hereof, saying that the City had anciently another name, which yet he expresses not; forbearing perhaps the word Magog, as sounding nothing elegantly in the Greek. But if we may believe Strabo, then was Edessa in Mesopotamia Mosopotamia the same Bambyce or Hierapolis, where the same Idol was worshipped. Ortelius is doubtful whether one of these Authors Authours did not mistake the place of this Bambyce or Hierapolis. It may well enough be that the same name and Religion was common to them both. Certain it is, that both of them lay due North from Palestine, and were both subject unto the Kings of the Race of Seleucus. Now I do not condemn the opinion of Hermolaus Barbarus following Josephus, but grant that perhaps Magog might also be the Father of the Scythians; notwithstanding that in this place, where Gog is made the Prince of Magog, the Nations of Coelesyria and the North parts adjoining be meant by Magog: for by a latter Plantation from these parts they might be propagated into Scythia. Yet it is not to be denied, that the Scythians in old times coming out of the Northeast wasted the better part of Asia the less, and possessed Coelesyria, where they built both Scythopolis and Hierapolis, which the Syrians call Magog. And that to this Magog 〈◊ 〉 had reference, it is very plain: for this City Hierapolis or Magog stands due North from Judea, according to the words of Ezekiel; that from the North quarters those Nations should come. For as the Kings of the South which infested the Israelites were the 〈◊ 〉 Kings of Egypt Aegypt: So those of the North were the Kings of Asia and Syria, the Successors of 〈◊ 〉, the Successor of Alexander Macedon. William Gulielmus Tyrius Tyrins thinks that this Hierapolis is that Rages, mentioned in the Story of Tobias. Pliny takes it not only to have been called Bambyce, as we have said, but also Edessa: not that by Euphrates; but another of the same name; now the known name is Aleppo Allepo: for So Bellonius expounds this Hierapolis, or Magog. This City had the title of Sacred, as the Sacred City, ( for So the word Hierapolis signifies) yet was it a place of most detested Idolatry, and wherein was worshipped the Idol of the Mermaid Atergatis, or Atirgitis, according to Pliny, which the Greeks call Derceto.

Now I do not condemn the opinion of Hermolaus Barbarus following Josephus, but grant that perhaps Magog might also be the Father of the Scythians; notwithstanding that in this place, where Gog is made the Prince of Magog, the Nations of Coelesyria and the North parts adjoining be meant by Magog: for by a latter Plantation from these parts they might be propagated into Scythia. Yet it is not to be denied, that the Scythians in old times coming out of the Northeast wasted the better part of Asia the less, and possessed Coelesyria, where they built both Scythopolis and Hierapolis, which the Syrians call Magog. And that to this Magog 〈◊ 〉 had reference, it is very plain: for this City Hierapolis or Magog stands due North from Judea, according to the words of Ezekiel; that from the North quarters those Nations should come. For as the Kings of the South which infested the Israelites were the 〈◊ 〉 Kings of Egypt: So those of the North were the Kings of Asia and Syria, the Successors of 〈◊ 〉, the Successor of Alexander Macedon. William Tyrius thinks that this Hierapolis is that Rages, mentioned in the Story of Tobias. Pliny takes it not only to have been called Bambyce, as we have said, but also Edessa: not that by Euphrates; but another of the same name; now the known name is Aleppo: for So Bellonius expounds this Hierapolis, or Magog. This City had the title of Sacred, as the Sacred City, ( for So the word Hierapolis signifies) yet was it a place of most detested Idolatry, and wherein was worshipped the Idol of the Mermaid Atergatis, or Atirgitis, according to Pliny, which the Greeks call Derceto.

p01229.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 4
p01229.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. IV, sig. 115b–116a
p01229.modern: If then we confer the words of Ezekiel in the third verse of the thirty eight Chapter, wherein he joins together Gog Meshech, and Tubal: and withal remember that Hierapolis was the City of Magog, which also is seated directly North from Judea: with whom also Ezekiel couples Gomer, and all his bands of the North quarters; we may( as I conceive) safely conclude, that these Followers and Vassals of Gog( which were Northern Nations in respect of Judea) were not the Gomerians of France, nor the Tubalines of Spain Spaine, but a people of the lesser Asia, and Coelesyria: and therefore that the opinions of Berosus, Josephus, and whosoever else has followed them therein are to be rejected. But if Josephus refer himself to later times, and think that some Colony of the Tubalines might from Iberia and Asia passe into Spain( to wit, from that piece of Land between Colchis( or Mengrelia) and Albania: ( most part possessed by the Georgians) then is his judgement of better allowance. For without any repugnancy of opinions, it may be granted, that in process of time these people might from their first habitation passe into the Countries near the Euxine Sea, and from thence in later ages into Spain.

p01231.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 4
p01231.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. IV, sig. 116a–116b
p01231.modern: But it is more probable, that Spain was first peopled by the Africans, who had ever since an affection to return thither, and to repeople it anew. This appeared by the Carthaginians of old, who were easily drawn to passe over the Straits Streights into that Country; and after by the Moors who held Granado, and the South parts eight hundred years, till the time of Ferdinand and Isabel. And either of these opinions are more probable, then that in the twelfth year of Nimrods reign, Tubal past into Spain, and therein built St. Vual: a poor Town, and a poor device, God knows. Certain it is that we must find Mosoch or Meshech, and Tubal neighbours, and Gomer and Togarma not far off, or else we shall wrong Ezekiel: for he called Gog the Leader or Prince of Meshech and Tubal, and makes Gomer and Togarmah their assistants. And that Meshech inhabited Asia, Funck Functius( though he followed Berosus) confesses, for these be his words: MESACUS MESACVS, qui ("Mesacus, who [was];") a Moses MOSE Meshech, priscos Mesios ab Adula monte usque ad Ponticam regionem posuit: haec regio postea Cappadocia dicta est, in qua 〈◊ 〉 Mazica, &c. haec est terra ("he placed the ancient Mysians from Mount Adula as far as the Pontic region: this region was afterwards called Cappadocia, in which [illegible] Mazica, etc. this is the land [of the Mysians];") MAGOG principalis. MESACUS, whom MOSES calls Meshech, placed the ancient Mesians from the mount Adulas, unto the coast of Pontus. This Region was afterward called Cappadocia, in which is the Town Mazica, &c. this is the principal Country of MAGOG. And this does Annius also avow, and yet forgets that Gog was Prince both of Meshech and Tubal: and therefore, that the one was a Nation of Spaniards, the other of Cappadocians, is very ridiculous; Spain lying directly West, and not North from Judea. Also Ezekiel in the 27. Chapter, where he prophesies of the destruction of Tyre, names Meshech and Tubal jointly. And for a final proof, that these Nations were of a Northern neighbour land( how far soever stretched) Ezekiel in the 38. Chapter makes them all horsemen. Thou, and much people with thee, all shall ride upon horses, even a great multitude and a mighty. Then if any man believe that these troupes came out of Spain over the Pyrenees Pyrenes, and first passed over a part of France, Italy Italie, Hungarie, and Sarmatia, and embarked again about the Hellespont, or else compassed all Pontus Euxinus, to come into the lesser Asia, which is half the length or compass of the then known World, he may be called a strong believer, but he shall never be justified thereby. But on the contrary it is known, that Seleucis was a Province neighbouring Palestine or Judea, and that Hierapolis( or Magog) joined unto it: whose Princes commanded all Syria, and Asia the less, ( namely the Seleucidae) and held it, till 〈◊ 〉 Asiaticus overthrew Antiochus the Great: after which they yet possessed Syria till the time of Tigranes: and whether Meshech be in Cappadocia, or under Iberia, yet is it of the Tubalines, and one and the same Dominion.

p01232.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 4
p01232.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. IV, sig. 116b
p01232.modern: Of Gomer the like may be said. First he seated himself with Togarmah, not far from Magog and Tubal, in the borders of Syria and Cilicia. Afterward he proceeded further into Asia the less; and in long tract of time his valiant issue filled all Germany, rested long in France and Brittaine, and possessed the utmost borders of the earth, accomplishing ( as Melanchthon Melancton well notes) the signification of their parents name, which is Utmost bordering. But when these borderers wanted further place, into which they might exonerate their swelling multitudes, that were bounded in by the great Ocean, then did they return upon the Nations occupying the Countries, through which they had formerly passed, oppressing first their Neighbours, afterwards the people more remote. Hereupon it was( as the worthy restorer of our antiquities, M. William Camden Cambden has noted) that they were called Cimbri, which in their old language does signify Robbers; necessity enforcing them to spoil their Neighbours, to whom in their original they were as near joined, as afterwards in the seats which they possessed. For that the warlike Nations of Germany Germanie were in elder ages accustomed to be beaten by the Gauls Gaules, the authority of Caesar affirming it is proof sufficient. But in times following they pursued richer conquests, and more easy though further distant, by which( to omit their other enterprises not here to be spoken of) they were drawn at length into Asia the less, and occupied those parts, which had formerly been held by their Progenitors. I say not that they claimed those Lands as theirs by descent; for likely it is, that they knew little of their own pedigree. Neither can any man therefore deny, that they were of old seated in Asia, because in late ages they returned thither; unless he will think, that all those Nations which from far parts have invaded and conquered the land of Shinar Shinaar, may by that argument be proved not to have issued from thence at the first.

p01233.modern: Now concerning Samothes for his excellent wisdom surnamed Dis, whom Annius makes the brother of Gomer and Tubal( which brother Moses never heard of, who spoke his knowledge of Japhets Iaphets sons) they must find him in some old Poet: for Funck, a great 〈◊ 〉, confesses: Quis hic SAMOTHES ("confesses: Who [is] this Samothes?") fuerit incertum est; Who this SAMOTHES was it is uncertain; neither is there any proof that he was that same Dis, whom Caesar says the 〈◊ 〉 suppose to be their Ancestor; yea, and Vigenère Vignier confesses with FUNCK: Mais on ne scayt qui il estoit; No man knows who he was.

p01235.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 5
p01235.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. V, sig. 116b–117a
p01235.modern: BUT before I go on with Noah his sons, I think it necessary to disprove the fiction which Annius has of Noah himself: an invention( indeed) very ridiculous, though warranted( as he has wrested) by those Authors of whom himself has Commented: as the Fragment of Berosus, Fabius, Pictor, Cato, Lavinius Lauinius and others. For Annius seeks to persuade us, that Noah( surnamed Janus) was the same which founded Genoa, with other Cities in Italy Italie, wherein he lived 92. years. This to disprove, by Moses silence, is a sufficient argument to me, if there were nothing else to disprove it. For if he vouchsafed to remember the building of Babel, Erec, Achad, Calneh Chalne and Nineveh Niniue by Nimrod, Noah was a man of too great mark to be forgotten, with all the acts he did in 92. years. But it were a needless labour for me to disprove the authority of that 〈◊ 〉, on whom Annius grounds, seeing So many learned Men have So demonstratively proved that Fragment to be counterfeit. Besides that, Tatianus the Assyrian in his Oration against the Greeks Greekes avows, that the ancient and true Berosus wrote only three Books, dedicated to Antiochus the successor of Seleucus Nicanor: but Annius has devised five Books Bookes, wherewith he honors Berosus. And whereas Berosus handled only the estate of the 〈◊ 〉 and Assyrians, Annius has filled this Fragment with the business of all the World. And if we may believe Eusebius better than Annius, then all the Kings of the Latins Latines ( before Aeneas) consumed but 150. years: whereas no man has doubted, but that from Noah to Aeneas arrival into Italy there past 1126.( after the least rate of the Hebrew account) and( after Codomannus Codoman) 1291. For Janus( who was the first of their Kings) lived at once with Ruth, who married Booz, in the Worlds year( as some reckon) 2717. after the Flood floud 1064. and Noah died 350. years after the 〈◊ 〉: and So there past between Janus of Italy and Noah surnamed Janus 704. years. For Saturn Saturnus succeeded Janus, Picus after Saturn, Faunus after Picus, and Latinus followed Faunus: which Latinus lived at once with 〈◊ 〉 the 27. King of Assyria; with Pelasgus of Peloponnesus; with Demophoon of Athens; and Sampson Judge of Israel. Now all these five Kings of the Latins having consumed but one hundred and fifty years; and the last of them in the time of Sampson: then reckoning upwards for one hundred and fifty years, and it reaches Ruth, with whom Janus lived.

p01236.modern: True it is, that the Greeks had their Janus; but this was not Noah: So had they Ion the son of Xuthus, the son of Deucalion, from whom they draw the Jones, who were indeed the children of Javan Iauan, the fourth son of Japheth Iapheth. For the vulgar translation( where the Hebrew word is Javan) writes Greece, and the Septuagint, Hellas; which is the same. So had they Medus the son of Medea, whom they make the parent of the Medes, though they were descended of a far more ancient Father( to wit) Madai the third son of Japheth.

p01237.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 5
p01237.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. V, sig. 117a
p01237.modern: Lastly, we see by a true experience, that the British language has remained among us above 2000. years, and the English speech ever since the invasion of the Angles, and the same continuance have all Nations observed among themselves, though with some corruption and alteration. Therefore, it is strange if either Noah( by them called Janus) had left in Italy his grand-child Gomer after him, or Tubal in Spain Spaine, that no plain resemblance of the Hebrew, Syrian, or Scythian( which no time could have quite extinguished) should have been found in the languages of those Countries. For which reasons we doubt not but these personal plantations of Janus, Gomer, Tubal, & c. in Italy, Spain, or France, are merely fabulous. Let the Italians therefore content themselves with the Grecian Janus, which commanded them and planted them, and who preceded the fall of 〈◊ 〉 but 150. years( says Eusebius) which was in the time of Latinus the fifth fift King: which also S. Augustine and Justin Iustine confirm: and this agrees with reason, time, and possibility. And if this be not sufficient to disprove this vanity, I may out of themselves ad thus much: That whereas some of them make 〈◊ 〉( others Camasena) the wife of this 〈◊ 〉, who instituted the holy 〈◊ 〉 of the Vestal Virgins in Rome( the 〈◊ 〉 and 〈◊ 〉 〈◊ 〉 from 〈◊ 〉 all their Idolatrous and Heathenish ceremonies) there is no man So impious, as to believe that 〈◊ 〉 himself( who is said by 〈◊ 〉 to 〈◊ 〉 〈◊ 〉 〈◊ 〉 God, to be a just man, and whom God of all mankind made choice of) could be either ignorant of the 〈◊ 〉 and only God, or So 〈◊ 〉 and ungrateful, to 〈◊ 〉 up or devise any Heathen salvage, or idolatrous 〈◊ 〉, or have instituted any ceremony, 〈◊ 〉 to that which he knew best pleasing to God himself.

p01239.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 6
p01239.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. VI, sig. 117b
p01239.modern: TO turn now to the sons of Noah, and the worlds plantation after the Flood floud: therein I observe, that as both reason and necessity taught them; So, when they multiplied in great numbers, and dispersed themselves into the next Countries bordering to their first habitations, & from thence sent forth Colonies elsewhere, it was in such a manner as that they might repair to each other, and keep intelligence by River: because the Land was yet Desert and over-pressed with Woods, Reeds Reedes, Bogs, and rotten Marshes Marishes. As when Nimrod seated in Babylonia, Cush Chus took the South part of Chaldea Chaldaea, down the River of Gihon Gehon, by which he might passe to and fro from Babylon to his own plantation: those also, which were of the race of Shem, inhabiting at Ur or Orchoa near the Lakes of Chaldea, might by the same River get up to Babylon, and receive succour from thence. All which Tract of Land upon 〈◊ 〉 Southward, Moses in the description of Paradise calls the Land of Cush: because the Dominion and Empire was then in the hands of Nimroda Cushite, by whom the children of Shem( which came into that Valley and stayed not in the East) were for a while oppressed, till God afterward by the seed of Abraham made them his own Nation and victorious. Havilah Hauilah, the brother of Nimrod, and son of Cush, took both banks of Tigris, especially on the East side of the River: by which River his people might also passe to and fro to Babel.

p01242.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 6
p01242.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. VI, sig. 118a
p01242.modern: The children of Tubal ranged as far as Iberia, to whom the Moschici were neighbours, which others write Meshech. The Prophet Ezekiel Ezechiel( coupling them together) calls Gog the Prince of Meschech and Tubal. For these Meschi( which Ptolemy calls Moschi) inhabit Syracena a Province of Armenia, directly South from the Mountains Moschici, in the Valley between the Mountains Moschici, and the Mountains Paryardes: out of whose North part springs the River Phasis; from the East part Araxis; and from the West Euphrates: and of this Meschech are descended also the Muscovites Moscouians( says Melanchthon Melanchton) and it may be, that in process of 〈◊ 〉 some of them inhabited those Regions also: For Meshech( says Melanchthon) 〈◊ 〉 extendens, enlarging or stretching forth. Togarmah also at first did inhabit amongst his parents and kindred. The Togormians were also called 〈◊ 〉, a people neighbouring the Sydonians in Gabala, a tetrarchy of 〈◊ 〉, the same which 〈◊ 〉 calls Gaben: from whence Solomon Salomon had his most excellent Masons, which hewed stones for the Temple of 〈◊ 〉. Thence the Togormians stretched into the less Armenia, whose Kings were hence called Tigranes, and their Cities 〈◊ 〉: of which Cities Tigranes subdued by Lucullus the Roman, built one. Hierosolymitanus has planted the Togormians in Barbary: forgetting the prophecy of Ezekiel against the Tyrians. They of the house of Togarmah, brought to thy Fayres horses, and horse-men, and mules, which could not well be driven over the whole length of the Mediterranean Mediterran Sea, but from the neighbour Countries by land. But Josephus Iosephus takes them for the parents of the Phrygians; which I do not deny, but they might be in the ensuing ages: and So might the Tubalines be of the Spaniards; but it was from Iberia, and many hundred years after the twelfth of Nimrods reign. The 〈◊ 〉 conceive that the Turks Turkes came of those Togormians, because their Emperor is called Togar. The 〈◊ 〉 make them the Fathers of the Germanes. But 〈◊ 〉 affirms, that the Turks descended of the Crimea Crim Tartar, which borders 〈◊ 〉. But for these subderivations it were infinite to examine them. Only of the first and second plantation, and of the first Nations after the Flood is the matter which I labour to discover; and therein to open the ignorance of some, and the corruption of other fabulous Writers. And this we must Note, that those grand-children of Noah which were of a more quiet, or( perchance) of less understanding, and had not therefore the leading of Colonies sent out, their proper habitations can be hardly known: only reason has taught us, that they dwelt among the rest, and were covered with the fame of others, who took on them the Conduction and Dominion over the rest.

p01245.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 7
p01245.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. VII, sig. 118a–118b
p01245.modern: OF Javan the fourth son of Japheth came the Jones, which were afterwards called the Greeks Greekes: and So the Latine and Greek Greeke Interpreters for Javan write Greece, as in Isa ESAT.: Et mittam ex 〈◊ 〉 qui 〈◊ 〉 fuerint ad gentes, in 〈◊ 〉, in Italiam, & Graeciam; And I will send those that escape of them to Nations in the Sea, in Italy Italie and in Greece. The Genevan Geneus here uses the word( Tarshish Tarshich) for Tarsus, a City in Cilicia, though Tarshish in many places be taken for the Sea. The Tigurine and the Geneva use the names Tubal and Javan, and not Italy and Greece: keeping the same Hebrew words. Of these Jones were the 〈◊ 〉, though themselves dream that they were 〈◊ 〉, or men without Ancestors Ancesters, and growing( as it were) out of the soil it self: who abounding in people sent Colonies into Asia the less, of whom came the Jones of those parts. Others derive the Athenians from Ion the son of Xuthus, the son of Deucalion; but the antiquity of Javan mars the fashion of that supposition, who So many years preceded Xuthus, Ion, or Deucalion. 〈◊ 〉 tells us that Xuthus stole out of Thessaly Thessalie with all his Fathers treasure, and his Brothers portions, and arriving at Athens, he was graciously received by Erechtheus Erictheus, who gave him his Daughter in marriage; of whom he received two sons, Ion, and Achaeus, the supposed Ancestors of the Athenians. For Attica was called Ionia( says Plutarch in the life of Theseus) who, when he had joined Megara to Attica, erected a pillar in that Isthmos or Strait, which fastens Peloponnesus to the other part of Greece: writing on that part which looks towards the East, these words: Haec non sunt Peloponnesus, ast Ionia ("These are not the Peloponnesus, but Ionia."); These Countries are not of Peloponnesus, but of Ionia: and on the other side which looked towards the South and into Peloponnesus, this: These parts are Peloponnesus, and not Ionia.

p01246.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 7
p01246.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. VII, sig. 118b
p01246.modern: Strabo out of Hecataeus affirms, that the Jones came out of Asia into Greece, which is contrary to the former opinion: That the Jones of Greece transporting certain companies into Asia the less, the name of Jones was thereby therein retained. And though Strabo knew no more thereof then he learned of the Greeks themselves, yet I find this conjecture of Hecataeus reasonable enough. For though it were to him unknown, yet sure I am that Asia the less had people before Greece had any: and that Javan did not fly from Babylonia into Greece, but took Asia the less in his passage; and from thence past over the nearest way, leaving his own name to some Maritime Province on that side, as he did to that part of Greece So called. But yet Strabo himself believed, that 〈◊ 〉 took the name from Ion the son of 〈◊ 〉: for So much he had learned from themselves; which was also the opinion of Pausanias. True it is, that the Greeks in after-times cast themselves into that part of Asia the less, opposite unto them, which they held for divers years. And howsoever the Greeks vaunt themselves to be the Fathers of Nations, and the most ancient; yet all approved Historians( not their own) deride and disprove their pride, and vanity therein. For this dispute of Antiquity( among profane Writers) rested between the 〈◊ 〉 and the Egyptians Aegyptians, as Justin Iustine out of Trogus, in the war between Vexoris of Egypt Aegypt, and Don Tanais of Scythia, witnesses: which preceded far the reign of Ninus, and was long before the name of Greece was ever heard of. And it is also manifest, that in Cecrops time the Greeks were all salvages without law or religion, living like brute beasts in all respects: and 〈◊ 〉( says S. Augustine) lived together with Moses.

p01247.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 7
p01247.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. VII, sig. 118b–119a
p01247.modern: The sixth son of Japheth was Meshech, whom the Septuagint cal Mosoch: ( a part of those Nations commanded by Gog the chief Prince of Meshech and Tubal. ) But this we must remember, that between Meshech Mesech the son of Aram, and Meshech( or Mosoch) the son of Japheth, there is little difference in name, and both by divers Interpreters diversely written. Montanus with the Vulgar writes Mesch, the son of Aram, Mes; the Geneva, Mash; Junius Iunius, Mesch. But it may be gathered out of the 120. Psalm, that either Meshech the son of Japheth, was the parent of those people, or gave name to that Province wherein David Dauid hid himself: or else( which may rather seem) that it took name from Mesch the son of Aram. For David bewailing his exile( while he lived among a barbarous and irreligious People) uses these words: Woe is me that I remain in Meshech, and dwell in the Tents of Kedar: which Junius converts thus: Hei mihi quia peregrinor tam 〈◊ 〉: habito tanquam Scenitae Kedareni: The Septuagint gives it this sense: Woe is me because my habitation( or abode) is prolonged, who dwell with the inhabitants of Kedar; with which this of the Latine agrees: Heu mihi, 〈◊ 〉 incolatus meus prolongatus est, 〈◊ 〉 cum habitantibus Kedar ("Woe is me, [illegible] my sojourning is prolonged, [illegible] with the inhabitants of Kedar:"): The Chaldean Chaldaean otherwise, and in these words: O me miserum, quia peregrinatus sum Asianis, habitavi cum taber 〈◊ 〉 Arabum; O wretch, that I am, for I have travailed among those of Asia: I have dwelt in the Tabernacles of the Arabians. But howsoever or which soever conversion be taken for the best, yet all make mention of Kedar: which is a Province of Arabia Petraea; and the Chaldean puts Asia in stead of Meshech, but the Hebrew itself has Meshech. And if it be to be taken for a Nation, ( as it is most likely, because it answers to Kedar, the name of a Nation) seeing Mesh the son of Aram, 1. Chron. 17. is called Meshech, it is indifferent whether this Nation took name from Meshech or Mesh, both bordering Judea Iudaea, and like enough to be commanded by one Prince; for So Ezekiel Ezechiel makes Meshech and Tubal. But as for those that take Meshech out of the word Mosoch( given by the Septuagint) to be the 〈◊ 〉: sure they presume much upon the affinity of names, as aforesaid. And sure I am that David never travailed So far North; ( for to him Muscovia Muscouia was utterly unknown) but about the border of Kedar( it may be) he was often in all the time of his persecution: the same being a City on the Mountains Mountaynes of Sanir or Gilead Galaad. And yet Arias Montanus makes Mosoch the father of the Muscovians Muscouians: and herein also Melanchthon Melanchton runs with the tide of common opinion, and sets Meshech in 〈◊ 〉, though with some better advice of judgement; as, first seated in Cappadocia, and from thence travailing Northward: expounding the places of the 120. Psalm, ( Hei 〈◊ 〉 quod exulo in Meshech) to signify, Gentis eius feritatem insignem esse; That the ferity of that Nation exceeded: which fierceness or brutality of the Muscovites Muscoutans, David never proved, or( perchance) never heard of. But the same ferity or cruelty which those Northern 〈◊ 〉 had, may as well be ascribed to the Arabians and Kedarens. For this Country took name of Kedar the second son of Ismael, of whom a people of equal fierceness to any of the World were begotten, both in those times and long after, even to this day( if the Arabians, 〈◊ 〉, and Saracens, may be accounted one people: ) the same being foreshowed by the speech of the Angel to Hagar, Gen. 16. v. 12. And he shall be a wild man: his hand shall be against every man, and every mans hand against him. Now Arabia the Desert( says Pliny Plinie) confronts the Arabians Cochlei on the East, and the Cedraei Southward, both which join together upon the 〈◊ 〉. So it appears( as before) that Meshech, Tubal, Gomer, Togarmah Togorma, and Magog, neighboured Canaan Canan and Israel, and that Kedar also did join to Meshech: all which were Regions of Syria, or of Asia the less, commanded by the Successors of Seleucus, enemies of the reestablishment of Israel and Judah Iuda. But( as I have already said) it might well be, that long after the first plantation the issue of Meshech( or Mosoch) might passe into Cappadocia, and thence into Hyrcania, and give names, both to 〈◊ 〉 in the one, and to the Mountains Moschici in the other, and from thence might send people more Northerly into 〈◊ 〉, and So all opinions saved. But all salvage Nations over-grown and uncultivated, do( for the most part) show a late plantation, even as Civility, Letters, and magnificent Buildings, witness antiquity.

For this Country took name of Kedar the second son of Ismael, of whom a people of equal fierceness to any of the World were begotten, both in those times and long after, even to this day( if the Arabians, 〈◊ 〉, and Saracens, may be accounted one people: ) the same being foreshowed by the speech of the Angel to Hagar, Gen. 16. v. 12. And he shall be a wild man: his hand shall be against every man, and every mans hand against him. Now Arabia the Desert( says Pliny) confronts the Arabians Cochlei on the East, and the Cedraei Southward, both which join together upon the 〈◊ 〉. So it appears( as before) that Meshech, Tubal, Gomer, Togarmah, and Magog, neighboured Canaan and Israel, and that Kedar also did join to Meshech: all which were Regions of Syria, or of Asia the less, commanded by the Successors of Seleucus, enemies of the reestablishment of Israel and Judah. But( as I have already said) it might well be, that long after the first plantation the issue of Meshech( or Mosoch) might passe into Cappadocia, and thence into Hyrcania, and give names, both to 〈◊ 〉 in the one, and to the Mountains Moschici in the other, and from thence might send people more Northerly into 〈◊ 〉, and So all opinions saved. But all salvage Nations over-grown and uncultivated, do( for the most part) show a late plantation, even as Civility, Letters, and magnificent Buildings, witness antiquity.

p01252.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. VIII, sig. 119b
p01252.modern: Eusebius makes Ashkenaz the Father of the Goths. The Jews Iewes in their Targum Thargum make him the root of the Germane Nation, but their expositions are commonly very idle. Pliny Plinie finds Ascania in Phrygia, near the Rivers Riuers of Hylas and Cios: Melanchthon Melanchton being of the same opinion, that the Tuiscones were descended of the Ashkenaz, ( for Tuiscones, says he, is as much to say, as of the Ashkenaz, praeposito articulo die Ashkenaz) and that the word signifies a Religious Keeper of fire: it being an ancient superstition to pray at the fire of Sacrifices, as afterwards at the Tombes of Martyrs. Not far from Phrygia was the Lake Ascania, known by that name in the Romans Romanes time. And among the Kings which came to the succour of Troy, was Ascanius( Deo similis ("Ascanius (like unto God"), says Homer) like 〈◊ 〉 God: because he was beautiful and strong: for in the same manner does Virgil grace Aeneas, Os humcrosque Deo similis, in face and body like one of the Gods. Virgil also remembers such a River together with the Hills Hils Gargara: as, Illas 〈◊ 〉 amor trans Gargara, transque sonantem ("[That] love [carries] them beyond Gargara, and beyond the sounding [sea];") ASCANIVM, Appetite leads them both over the Mountains Mountaines Gargara, and the roaring ASCANIVS. But this Pliny makes more plain in the description of Phrygia. For he places the City of Brillion upon the River 〈◊ 〉, which is adjoining to 〈◊ 〉. and is near the border of the 〈◊ 〉 Empire: and the Lake Ashkenaz he directs us to find by the description of Prusia, founded by Hannibal at the foot of Olympus, which Iyeth far within the Countries of Bithynia: and then from 〈◊ 〉 to 〈◊ 〉 are accounted five and twenty miles, in which way this Lake lies, even between 〈◊ 〉 and Nicaea Nicea. And So 〈◊ 〉( as I conceive him) takes them of Ashkenaz, to be the inhabitants of Pontus, and Bithynia, and those North parts of Asia. Stephanus de 〈◊ 〉 makes it a City of Troas, built by 〈◊ 〉 the son of Aeneas: saying, that there was another of that name in Mysia. Of Ascania a Lake of Bithynia, Ptolemy Ptolomie witnesses: and Strabo gives Ascania both a Lake, a River, and a Town in Mysia, near unto Cio; which also agrees with Pliny. For Pliny finds Prusia( before spoken of) near Cio, and calls the Islands before Troy Ascanes.

p01253.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 8
p01253.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. VIII, sig. 119b–120a
p01253.modern: Now, whether these places took name of 〈◊ 〉 the son of Gomer, or of Ascanius the son of Aeneas, it might be questioned: sure it is, that Ascanius which brought succour to the Trojans Troians, could not take his name from Aeneas son, who was then either exceeding young, or rather unborn: and it seems that the Countries whence those succours came, were not out of any part of Phrygia or Mysia, but farther off, and from the North parts of all Asia the less, which by Jeremiah Hieremie is called Ashkenaz, by the figure Synecdoche, as 〈◊ 〉 thinks. Out of those testimonies therefore which deceive not, we may confidently determine. For of the Prophet Jeremiah we shall learn of what Nation the Ascenez were, whose words are these: Set up a Standard in the Land, blow the Trumpet among the Nation against her, call up the Kings of Ararat, 〈◊ 〉, and Ashkenaz against her, & c. meaning against the 〈◊ 〉. Ararat was Armenia the greater, as most Interpreters consent, So called of the Mountains of Ararat which run through it: Minni the lesser Armenia: Armenia being compounded of Aram and Minni. For Minni was the ancient name: ( says Junius Iunius and others before him) and Aram anciently taken for Syria, which contained all that Tract from Euphrates to the Sea-coasts of Phoenicia and Palestine Palaestina; and therefore 〈◊ 〉 being in elder times but a Province of Syria, the Scriptures difference it in the Story of 〈◊ 〉 and 〈◊ 〉, and call it Aram-padam. Then if these two Nations were of the 〈◊ 〉, and 〈◊ 〉 joined with them( who altogether united under Cyrus and Darius, came to the spoil of the Babylonian Empire) we shall er much to call Askenaz Germany Germanie or Almain, for we hear of no Swart Routiers Ruttiers at that siege. But the Askenaz were of those Nations which were either subject or allied to the Medes: of which, if any of them came afterward into Phrygia, I know not: for the dispersion of Nations was in aftertimes without account. But for the opinion of 〈◊ 〉, who makes them to be Goths; or that of Josephus, who calls them Rhegini; or of the Jews, who will have them to be Germans Almaines; when they confirm it either by Scriptures or Reason, I will think as they do.

p01254.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 8
p01254.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. VIII, sig. 120a
p01254.modern: Of Riphath the second son of Gomer there is mention in the first of Chronicles. Beroaldo Beroaldus and Pereira Pererius think that he wandered far off from the rest of his Brothers, and therefore no memory of his plantation. But I see nothing to the contrary, but that he might seat himself with the rest of his Family: for there wanted no room or soil in those days for all the sons and Grand-children of Noah. Therefore I take it to be well understood, that the Riphei were of Riphath, which the Greeks afterwards( according to Josephus) called the Paphlagonians Paphlagones: and Riphei( says Melanchthon) signifies Giants. These people were very famous in the North parts, and in Sarmatia: the most of number and power among them, Sarmatarum gens maxima Heneti, The greatest number of the Sarmatians were the Heneti; who spoke the ancient Polish Polac: which being first called Riphei( for the love of some of their Leaders or Kings) changed their names and became Heneti, ( a custom exceeding common in those times) and dwelt first in Paphlagonia, as Homer witnesses, and So does Apollonius in his Argonautica Argonauticks: Now, when these Rephei( afterward Heneti) sought new Regions, they came along the shores of Euxinus, and filled the North part of Europe, containing Russia, Lituania, and Polonia. From thence they crossed thwart the Land, and peopled Illyria, desirous( says Melanchthon) of a warmer soil of fruit and Wine. These Heneti or Veneti, whom Melanchthon takes to be one people, filled all that Land between the Baltic and Adriatic Sea; and to this day the name of the Gulf Venedicus is found in Russia. This Nation, after they were possessed of Lituania and Polonia, disturbed the plantation of the Boii Boij and Hermunduri Hermondurij. Therefore, it seems to me, that of Riphath came the Riphei, afterward Heneti; and So thinks Arias Montanus, first seated in Paphlagonia, but in course of time Lords of Sarmatia, and those other parts before remembered, chiefly between the Rivers of Vistula and Elbe Albis. The name( says Melanchthon) signifies wandering or Wanderers, or Nomads Nomades: a people which lived by White-meats White-meates and fruits, as( indeed) all Nations did in the first Ages.

p01258.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 9
p01258.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. IX, sig. 120a–120b
p01258.modern: OF Elisa or Elishah Elipha, came the Aeoles: and of this Elisa all the Greeks Greekes were called Hellenes, says Montanus. Melanchthon Melanchton makes Elisa the Father of the Aeoles in Asia side: others of Elis in Peloponnesus, or of both. And seeing the Greeks were descended in general of Javan, it is probable that the Aeoles and the Elei, took name of Elisa, his eldest Son. Ezekiel Ezechiel in the 27. speaking of Tyre, names the Isles of Elisa. Hyacynthus & purpur a de insulis Elisae facta sunt operimentum tuum: Blue Silk and Purple, brought from the Isles of Elisa, was thy covering: The Chaldeans Chaldaeans for Elisa write Italia: but the Vulgar, the Tigurine, the Geneva, and Junius Iunius, keep the word Elisa: and So I think they might do with reason. For there was not found any such Purple Dye in Italy Italie in those days nor since, that I can read of: but those Isles of Elisa, were by a better conjecture the Isles of Greece; and the best Purple was found afterward at Tyre it self e and before that, among the Cyclades, and on the Coast of Getulia.

p01259.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 9
p01259.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. IX, sig. 120b
p01259.modern: Tarshish, the second Son of Javan, inhabited Cilicia, of which Tarshish is the Metropolis. Montanus for Tarshish in Cilicia, understands Carthage in Africa; but( reserving the respect due to So learned a man) he was much mistaken in that conjecture. The Chaldean Chaldaean Paraphrast puts Carthage for Tarshish, but it has no authority, nor warrant of reason therein. So likewise, where it is written, that the Ships of Solomon Salomon went every three years to Tarshish, and brought thence Gold, Silver, Elephants teeth, &c. the Chaldean Paraphrast translates Tarshish( Africa. ) But Salomons Ships were prepared in the Red Sea at Esion Gaber, in the Bay of Elana, near unto Midian Madian, where Jethro( Moses Father in Law) inhabited; a Province of Arabia Petraea, Idumea Idumaea, or of the Cushites Chusites; and they sailed to the higher part of the East India. For it had been a strange Navigation to have spent three years in the passage between Judea Iudaea and Carthage, or any other part of Africa, which might have been sailed in six or ten days. And if So great riches might have been found within the bounds of the Mediterranean Mediterran Sea, all other neighbouring Princes would soon have entertained that Trade also. But this enterprise of Solomon is in this sort written of in the first of Kings: Also King Solomon Made a Navy of Ships in Esion Gaber, which is beside Elath and the brink of the Red Sea in the Land of Edom: and HYRAM sent with the Navy his servants, that were Mariners, and had knowledge of the Sea, with the servants of Solomon: and they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence 420. Talents of Gold, &c. But as the Nations about Pontus thought no Sea in the World like unto their own, and doubted whether there were any other Sea but that only: ( whereof it came, that Pontus was a word used for the Sea in general) So, because the Israelites and the Phoenicians knew no other Sea then that of the Mediterranean in the beginning; and that the people of Tarshish had the greatest Ships, and were the first Navigators Nauigators in those parts with such Vessels, they were therefore called men of the Sea: and the word Tarshish used often for the Sea. And whereas it is said that the Ships of Solomon went every three years to Tarshish, that phrase is not strange at all; for we use it ordinarily wheresoever we navigate, ( namely) that the Kings Ships are gone to the Sea, or that they are set out every year, or every three year to the Sea, and therefore Tarshish was not therein named, either for Carthage, Africa, or India, but used for the Sea it self. But in this place Tarshish is truly taken for Tarshish, the chief City in Cilicia, founded by Tarshish the second son of Javan, or by his Successors Successours in memory of their first parent. To this City arrived Alex. Macedon, before he gave the first overthrow to Darius, and casting himself into the River to bathe and wash his body, he fell into an extreme Fever, and great danger of death: and in this City of Tarshish was Saint Paul borne. Now this agrees with the reason and nature of a Plantation. For( Gomer and his other sons inhabiting Asia the less, and that part of Syria adjoining) Javan, who was to passe over the Sea into Greece, took the edge of the same Coast, and first planted the Jones on that shore: gave the Islands between Asia the less and Greece, to Elisa, and left Tarshish upon the Sea-side in Cilicia; of whom that City took name.

p01260.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 9
p01260.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. IX, sig. 120b–121a
p01260.modern: The third son of Javan was Kittim Cethim, of whom were the Romans and Italians, says 〈◊ 〉, but I allow better of Melanchthon's Melanchtons opinion, who makes Kittim the Father of the Macedonians. Kittim is a voice plural( says he) and signifies percussors, though in that respect it may be meant by either. But it seems more probable, that the place of Isa Esai.. 23. ( according to Melanchthon) had relation to Alexander and the Macedonians: Hac calamitas ab Isa. praedicta est, quicapite vicessimo tertio inquit, 〈◊ 〉 esse eversores Tyriex terra Cittim, This calamity( says Melanchthon) was foreshowed by Isa. the Prophet, who in the three and twentieth Chapter pronounced, that the Destroyers of Tyre were to come out of Cittim. p01261.modern: Dodanim the fourth son of Javan, and the youngest Brother( by the most opinions) sate down at Rhodes, as near Kittim, Tarshish, and Elisa, as he could. For Dodanim and Rhodanim are used indifferently by many Translators: the Hebrew( D) and the Hebrew( R) are So like, as the one may easily be taken for the other, as all Hebraists Hebricians affirm. There is also found in Epirus the City of Dodona, in the Province of Molossia. And as Kittim, when he wanted soil in Cyprus: So Dodanim( seated in a far less Island) did of necessity send his people farther off; and keeping along the Coast, and finding Peloponnesus in the possession of Elisa, he passed a little farther on the Westward, and planted in Epirus. And though the City of Dodona was not then built, or( perchance) not So ancient as Dodanim himself, yet his Posterity might give it that name in memory of their first parent, as it happened all the World over. For names were given to Cities, Mountains Mountaines, Rivers Riuers, and Provinces Prouinces, after the names of Noahs children, and grand-children; not in all places by themselves, but by their successors many years after: every of their Families being desirous to retain among them by those memories, out of what branch themselves were taken, and grafted elsewhere. And because great Kingdoms Kingdomes were often by new Conquerers newly named, and the greatest Cities often fired and demolished: therefore those that hoped better to perpetuate their memories, gave their own names, or the names of their Ancestors, to Mountains and Rivers, as to things( after their judgements) freest from any alteration.

p01266.modern: That Ham was the Father of the Egyptians, it is made manifest in many Scriptures, as in the 105. Psalm verse 51. Then ISRAEL came to Egypt, and Jacob IACOB was a stranger in the land of HAM: and in the 78. Psalm, He slew all the first-borne in Egypt, even the beginning of their strength, in the Tabernacles of HAM. There is also found a great City in Thebaida, called Cheramis: ( as it were the City of Ham) of which name 〈◊ 〉 also discovers an Island in the same Region. But because Cush is the elder son of Ham, it agrees with order to speak first of him. Now though I have already in the description of Paradise handled this question, and( I hope) proved that Cush could not be Ethiopia: yet seeing it comes now to his turn to speak for himself, I will ad some farther proof to the former. For the manifestation hereof sets many things straight, which had otherwise very crooked constructions, and senseless Interpretations. Surely, how soever the Septuagint and Josephus have herein failed, yet it is manifest that Cush could not be Ethiopia, but Arabia: ( to wit) both that Arabia called Petraea, and a part of Arabia the Happy and the Desert: which Regions Cush and the Cushites Chusites presently planted, after they left Babylonia to Nimrod, wherein they first sate down altogether. And there is nothing which So well clears this Controversy, as the true interpretation of the place, Num. 12. v. 1. where Moses his Wife is called a Chusite; together with some places which speak of Nebuchadnezzar's Nabuchodonosors Conquests. For whereas Josephus and the Septuagint in the place, Num. 12. v. 1. as also elsewhere, understand Cush for Ethiopia, we must give credit to Moses himself herein; and then it will appear that Josephus was grossly mistaken, or vainly led by his own invention. For Josephus presuming that Cush was Ethiopia, and therefore that the Wise of Moses( which in Scripture, Num. 12. verse 1. is called a woman of Cush) was a woman of the land of Ethiopia, feigns that Tharbis the Daughter of the King of Ethiopia, fell in love with the person and fame of Moses, while he besieged Sheba Saba her Fathers City; and to the end, to obtain Moses for her Husband, she practised to betray both her Parents, Country, and friends, with the City it self, and to deliver it into Moses hands. The Tale( if it be worth the reciting) lies thus in Josephus. After he had described the strength of the Ethiopian Aethiopian City Meroe, which he says at length Cambyses called So from the name of his Sister, ( the old name being Sheba) he goes on in these words: Hic cum ("Here, when [he];") MOSES desidere exercitum 〈◊ 〉 aegre ferret, hoste non audente manus 〈◊ 〉, tale quiddam accidit. Erat 〈◊ 〉 Regi 〈◊ 〉, nomine ("The army [illegible] bore with difficulty, the enemy not daring to join battle [illegible], something of this sort happened. There was [illegible] to the king [illegible], named…") THARBIS, & c. which Tale has this sense in English: When MOSES was 〈◊ 〉 that his Army lay idle, because the Enemy besieged, durst not sally and come to handy strokes, there happened this accident in the mean while. The Ethiopian King had a Daughter called THARBIS, who at some 〈◊ 〉 given beheld the person of MOSES, and withal admired his valour. And knowing that MOSES had not only up-held and restored the falling estate of the Egyptians, but had also brought the conquering 〈◊ 〉 to the very brink of subversion: these things working in her thoughts, together with her own affection, which daily increased, she made means to send unto him by one of her trustiest servants to offer her self unto him, and become his Wife; Which MOSES on this condition entertained, that she should first deliver the City into his possession: where unto she 〈◊ 〉, and MOSES having taken oath to perform 〈◊ 〉 contract, both the one and the other were instantly performed.

p01268.section: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. 10
p01268.citation: Book I, Part I, Chapter VIII, §. X, subsection II, sig. 122a–122b
p01268.modern: This Tale( whereof Moses has not a word) has Josephus fashioned, and therein also utterly mistaken himself, in naming a City of Arabia for a City of Ethiopia: as he names Ethiopia itself to have been the Country of Moses his Wife, when( indeed) it was Arabia. For Sheba is not in Ethiopia, but in Arabia, as both Strabo and all other Geographers, ancient and modern teach us, saying that the Sabaeans are Arabians and not Ethiopians Aethiopians; except Josephus can persuade us, that the Queen of Sheba which came from the South to hear the wisdom of Solomon Salomon, were a Negro, or Black-Moore Blacke-Moore. And though Damianus a Goes speak of certain Letters to the King of Portugal from Prester John Iohn, of the Abyssinians Abissines: wherein that Ethiopian King would persuade the Portugals that he was descended of the Queen of Sheba, and of Solomon; yet it does no where appear in the Scriptures, that Solomon had any Son by that great Princess: which had it been true, it is likely that when Shishak Sishac King of Egypt invaded Roboam, and sacked Jerusalem Hierusalem, his Brother( the Son of Sheba and Solomon) who joined upon Egypt, would both have impeached that enterprise, as also given aide and succour to Roboam against Jeroboam Ieroboam, who drew from him ten of the twelve Tribes to his own obedience. Neither is it any thing against our opinion of Moses his Wife, to have been an Arabian, that the Scriptures teach us, that Moses married the daughter of Jethro Priest of Midian or Midian Madian: which standing on the North Coast of the Red Sea, over against the body of Egypt, and near Esion Gaber, where Solomon provided his Fleet for India, in the Region of Edom, may well be reckoned as a part of Arabia, as the Red Sea is called Sinus Arabicus. For Idumea Edumaea joins to the Tribe of Judah Iuda by the North, to Arabia Petraea by the East, to the Mediterranean Mediterran by the West, and to the Red Sea by the Southeast. And if we mark the way which Moses took when he left Egypt, and conducted Israel thence, it will appear that he was no stranger in Arabia: in the border whereof, and in Arabia itself, he had formerly lived forty years; where it seems, that besides his careful bringing up in Egypt, he was instructed by Jethro in the Egyptians learning. For Josephus confesses, and Saint Stephen confirms, that he was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians. But on the other side this Text makes much against Josephus, where it is written in Exodus the second, Therefore MOSES fled from Pharaoh PHARAO, and dwelt in the Land of Midian or Midian, and not in Ethiopia. And in the third Chapter it is as plain as words can express, in what Region Midian was, where it is written, When MOSES kept the sheep of JETHRO his Father in Law, Priest of Midian, and drove the Flock to the Desert, and came to the Mountain of GOD in 〈◊ 〉. Now that Mount Horeb is not in Ethiopia, every Infant knows. And if we may believe Moses himself, then was not the Wife of Moses purchased in that manner which Josephus reports( which was for betraying her Country and Friends) neither had she the name of Tharbis, but of Zipporah Sippora, or Zippora: neither was she a Negro, but a Madianitish. And as God works the greatest things by the simplest means: So it pleased him from a Shepherd to call Moses, and after him David Dauid, and by them to deliver his people first and last. For Moses sitting by a Well( as disconsolate and a stranger) defended the daughters of Reuel Reguel from the other shepherds, and drew them Water to water their sheep: upon which occasion( by God ordained) he was entertained by 〈◊ 〉, whose Daughter he married: and not for any betraying of Towns Townes or Countries.

p01269.modern: From hence also came Jethro to Moses at 〈◊ 〉, not far from Idumea, and finding the insupportable government of such a multitude, he advised him to distribute this weighty charge, and to make Governors Gouernours and Judges Iudges of every Tribe and Family. And if Jethro had been an Ethiopian, it had been a far progress for him to have passed through all Egypt with the Wife and Children of Moses, and to have found Moses in the border of 〈◊ 〉: the Egyptians hating Moses and all that favoured him. But the passing of Moses through Arabia Petraea( which joins to Midian) proves that Moses was well acquainted in those parts: in which the second time he wandered forty years, and did by these late travails of his, seek to instruct the children of Israel in the knowledge of one true God, before he brought them to the Land of plenty and rest. For he found them nourished up with the milk of Idolatry, and obstinate in the Religion of the Heathen, and finding that those stiff plants could not be bowed or declined, either by persuasion or by miracle, he ware them out in the Deserts Desarts, as God directed, and grafted their branches a new, that from those he might receive fruit, agreeable to his own desire, and Gods Commandments Commandements.

p01270.modern: Lastly, this opinion of Josephus is condemned by Augustinus Chrisamensis, where also he reprehends Apollinaris, who avowed that Moses had married both Tharbis and Sephora: His own words have this beginning: Mentitur ettam APOLLINARIS duas uxores habuisse ("to have had two wives") MOSEN, &c. APOLLINARIS also lies in affirming that MOSES had two wives: and who does not perceive these things feigned by them? for it is 〈◊ 〉 that the wife of MOSES was Zipporah, Daughter to the Priest or President of Midian: and that Midian cannot be taken for Ethiopia beyond Egypt; being the same that joins to Arabia: So far Chrisamensis.
